## Sea Ice Data: Extraction

This script extracts sea ice concentration (sic) data from the 16 pixels (each 25 km x 25 km) in the northern Bering Sea identified in Petersen and Douglas (2004) as spectacled eider winter range, based on satellite transmitter locations from the 1990s. These 16 pixels are used as an index of sea ice conditions across the broader area of the Bering Sea used by spectacled eiders, following Petersen and Douglas (2004), Flint et al. (2016), Christie et al. (2018), Dunham et al. (2021), and Friendly et al. (2025).

The output is a daily time series of sic (percent cover, 0 to 100) at each of the 16 pixels, for each winter (01 Nov to 30 Apr) day falling within the requested date range.

This script was adapted from code posted by A. Fischbach, modified by G. Durner in 2020, and updated by D. Rizzolo in 2020.

Data are SMMR and SSM/I Passive Microwave SIC from the Bootstrap Algorithm, version 4.0 (released November 2023):

This script processes all GeoTIFFs within a specified date range (`start_date` to `end_date`, set below) and appends that data to the existing cumulative data set spanning all previously processed winters, if one exists.

## Work flow

This is the third script in a four-script workflow. The raw data are downloaded here with this `00_download_seaice_data_from_nsidc.Rmd` script, converted from the native netCDF format to GeoTIFFs with `01_convert_netcdf_to_geotif.Rmd`, then extracted from the pixels of interest using the current `02_extract_specEider_winterice_bootstrap_sic_geotif.Rmd` script, and finally summarized into annual sea ice variables with `03_summarize_daily_min_bs3_sic.Rmd`.

### Inputs

- **Pixel coordinate reference file**: `library/specEider_winter_pixel_samples_xy_geo_SAVE.csv` - longitude/latitude (WGS84) coordinates of the 16 spectacled eider winter-range pixels. This is a reference file, that isn't changed and is unrelated to the date range below.
- **Input directory of daily GeoTIFFs**: `data/sourced_data/nsidc_sic_v4/sic_geotif/sic_geotif_[start_date]_[end_date]/` - versioned by date range to match the output of `01_convert_netcdf_to_geotif.Rmd`, using the same `start_date`/`end_date` parameters defined below. One file per day, named `NSIDC0079_SEAICE_PS_N25km_[YYYYMMDD]_v4.0.tif`. The file list is filtered to `.tif` files only, to avoid picking up ancillary files that get written alongside the GeoTIFFs. The date and month are parsed from fixed character positions within this filename (positions 27-34 for the full date, 31-32 for the month), so input files must follow this exact naming convention and length for those extractions to return the correct characters.
- **`start_date`/`end_date` parameters** (defined in `define_params` below): scope which GeoTIFFs in the input directory are actually extracted - a file is only processed if its embedded date falls within this range (inclusive) and its month is Nov-Apr. For the complete available time series, use `start_date = "1992-11-01"` and `end_date = "2025-04-30"`.
- **`previous_cumulative_end_date` parameter**: the ending date of an existing cumulative output file, if one exists, that this run should load and extend. If no file exists at the resulting path, this script treats the current run's output as the starting point for a new cumulative file, rather than causing an error
- **`overwrite_existing` parameter**: controls what happens if an output file this script would write already exists at that exact path (see "Outputs" and the `safe_write_csv` helper below for details).

Spatial data references used in this script:

- EPSG:3411 - NSIDC Sea Ice Polar Stereographic North (the projection of the sea ice GeoTIFFs; assigned during conversion in `01_convert_netcdf_to_geotif.Rmd`)
- EPSG:4326 - WGS 84 Geographic (the projection of the pixel coordinate reference file)

```{r define_params, warning = FALSE}
# Define analysis parameters ####

start_date <- as.Date("1992-11-01") # earliest date to extract (inclusive)
end_date   <- as.Date("2025-04-30") # latest date to extract (inclusive)

# Ending date of an existing cumulative output file to load and extend, if one exists.
# If no file exists at the resulting path (see append_full_dataset below),
# this output becomes the starting point for a new cumulative file instead.
previous_cumulative_end_date <- as.Date("2024-04-30")

# Versioned input directory, matching the output path convention used in
# 01_convert_netcdf_to_geotif.Rmd (same start_date/end_date format)
geotif_dir <- path_abs(glue("data/sourced_data/nsidc_sic_v4/sic_geotif/sic_geotif_{format(start_date, '%Y%m%d')}_{format(end_date, '%Y%m%d')}"))

# Output directory and naming root for both the single-period and cumulative CSVs
output_dir <- "output/sic_beringSea_16pixels"

# Set to TRUE to allow overwriting an existing output file (a timestamped backup
# of the existing file is made automatically first - see safe_write_csv below).
# Default FALSE: any write that would overwrite an existing file stops with an
# error instead, so accidental overwrites require a deliberate opt-in.
overwrite_existing <- FALSE
```

```{r safe_write_helper, echo = FALSE, warning = FALSE}
# Write a CSV without silently overwriting an existing file ####
# If destfile already exists:
#   - overwrite_existing == FALSE (default): stop with an error, write nothing.
#   - overwrite_existing == TRUE: rename the existing file aside with a
#     timestamped ".bak_[timestamp]" suffix, then write the new file in its place.
# This applies to both output writes in this script (single-period and cumulative).

safe_write_csv <- function(df, destfile, overwrite = overwrite_existing) {
  if (file_exists(destfile)) {
    if (!overwrite) {
      stop(glue(
        "File already exists and overwrite_existing is FALSE - refusing to overwrite:\n  {destfile}\n",
        "Set overwrite_existing <- TRUE in define_params to allow this (a timestamped backup will be made automatically)."
      ))
    }
    backup_path <- glue("{destfile}.bak_{format(Sys.time(), '%Y%m%d_%H%M%S')}")
    file_move(destfile, backup_path)
    cat(glue("Existing file backed up to: {backup_path}\n"))
  }
  write.csv(df, destfile, row.names = FALSE)
  cat(glue("Saved: {destfile}\n"))
}
```

```{r load_pixel_coords, warning = FALSE}
# spatial data references used here:
#* EPSG:3411: NSIDC Sea Ice Polar Stereographic North
#* EPSG:4326: WGS 84 Geographic

# make Sea Ice Concentration (SIC) grid cell reference coordinates spatial with st_as_sf from package sf and reproject to same CRS as sea ice data
eider16.geo <- read.csv("library/specEider_winter_pixel_samples_xy_geo_SAVE.csv") # Read CSV into a regular data frame
eider16.sf <- st_as_sf(eider16.geo, coords = c("lon", "lat"), crs = 4326) # Convert to an sf object with WGS84 coordinates (EPSG:4326)
eider16.ps <- st_transform(eider16.sf, crs = 3411) # Reproject to NSIDC Sea Ice Polar Stereographic North (EPSG:3411)
```

## Extraction

For each daily GeoTIFF in the input directory whose embedded date falls within `start_date` to `end_date` and whose month is Nov-Apr, this script loads the raster, extracts the sic value at each of the 16 reprojected pixel locations, and appends the result (with date, projected x/y coordinates, and original lon/lat) to a running list of daily data frames. All other files are skipped. Any file that fails to load or extract is logged to `error_log` and skipped, rather than stopping the whole run.

```{r list_input_files, warning = FALSE}
# get a list of the geotif files converted from NetCDF in 01_convert_netcdf_to_geotif.Rmd
dir_exists(geotif_dir)

tif.list <- as.list(list.files(path = geotif_dir, pattern = "\\.tif$"))
eider_list <- list() # Initialize list to collect daily data frames
```

```{r extract_loop, warning = FALSE}
# code applied to GeoTIFFs within start_date to end_date (set in define_params above)

# create progress bar (works when code is run piece by piece, but not when knitting)
pb <- progress_bar$new(
  format = "  Converting [:bar] :percent | :current/:total | :filename", # pb layout
  total = length(tif.list), # total files
  clear = FALSE, # keep bar visible until loop finishes
  width = 60 # displayed bar width
)

error_log <- list() # collect any files that fail to load/extract, with the associated error message

# loop through directory of geotif files
for (f in tif.list) {
  pb$tick(tokens = list(filename = f)) # progress bar by 1 step each file
  file_date <- as.Date(substr(f, 27, 34), format = "%Y%m%d") # parse full date from file name (example: "NSIDC0079_SEAICE_PS_N25km_20211114_v4.0.tif")
  month <- as.numeric(format(file_date, "%m"))
  # Process only files within the requested date range, and only Nov-Apr
  if (!is.na(file_date) && file_date >= start_date && file_date <= end_date && (month >= 11 || month <= 4)) {
    tryCatch({
      # load raster using terra
      filename <- file.path(geotif_dir, f) # assign file name with path
      rr <- terra::rast(filename)
      # extract sea ice values at point locations for 16 eider pixels of interest
      values <- terra::extract(rr, vect(eider16.ps))[,2]  # second column is the ice value
      # get coordinates from sf object
      coords <- sf::st_coordinates(eider16.ps)
      colnames(coords) <- c("x", "y") # rename columns upper- to lowercase
      # create data frame
      eider16p <- eider16.ps %>%
        st_drop_geometry() %>% # remove the geometry column of the sf object
        # add column for:
        mutate(bs_sic_prop = values, # sea ice concentration 
               sicDate = substr(f, 27, 34), # extract date from file name, positions 3 to 10
               x = coords[, "x"], # EPSG 3411 x values
               y = coords[, "y"]
               ) %>% # EPSG 3411 y values
        # join the original lat/lon columns from eider16.geo by row index
        dplyr::bind_cols(
          eider16.geo %>% dplyr::select(lon, lat)
        )
      # append to list
      eider_list[[length(eider_list) + 1]] <- eider16p # append daily values
    }, error = function(e) {
      error_log[[length(error_log) + 1]] <<- list(file = f, message = conditionMessage(e))
    })
  }
}

if (length(error_log) > 0) {
  cat(glue::glue("\n{length(error_log)} file(s) failed to extract:\n"))
  for (err in error_log) {
    cat(glue::glue("  {err$file}: {err$message}\n"))
  }
} else {
  cat(glue::glue("\nAll {length(eider_list)} file(s) extracted without errors.\n"))
}
```

## Combine and inspect

```{r combine_and_inspect, warning = FALSE}
# call bind rows to combine all daily data frames into data frame eider16p
eider16p <- dplyr::bind_rows(eider_list)

# output is eider16p, take a look
str(eider16p)
summary(eider16p$bs_sic_prop)
```

## Save output

The single-period output file is named using `start_date` and `end_date`. If a file already exists at the target path, `safe_write_csv()` either refuses to overwrite it (default) or backs it up first, depending on `overwrite_existing`.

```{r save_output, warning = FALSE}
# save reprocessed time series
single_period_file <- file.path(output_dir, glue("sic_bootstrapv4_16pixels_{format(start_date, '%Y%m%d')}_{format(end_date, '%Y%m%d')}.csv"))
safe_write_csv(eider16p, single_period_file)
```

## Append to full multi-year data set

The newly processed data (`eider16p`) is appended to the existing cumulative record, if one exists at the path implied by `start_date` and `previous_cumulative_end_date`. If no such file exists (e.g. this is the first run covering the complete series), `eider16p` becomes the full cumulative data set directly. The combined result is saved as a new file named with `start_date` and `end_date`, again using `safe_write_csv()` to avoid silently overwriting a prior cumulative file of the same name.

```{r append_full_dataset, warning = FALSE}
# Build path to the existing cumulative file, if one exists ####
previous_cumulative_file <- file.path(
  output_dir, "nsidc_sic_summary_v4",
  glue("sic_bootstrapv4_16pixels_01Nov-30Apr_{format(start_date, '%Y')}-{format(previous_cumulative_end_date, '%Y')}.csv")
)

if (file_exists(previous_cumulative_file)) {
  cat(glue("Loading existing cumulative file: {previous_cumulative_file}\n"))
  all_previous <- read.csv(previous_cumulative_file)
  bind <- rbind.data.frame(all_previous, eider16p)
} else {
  cat(glue("No existing cumulative file found at: {previous_cumulative_file}\n"))
  cat("Treating this run's output as the starting point for a new cumulative file.\n")
  bind <- eider16p
}

# check and remove duplicate records
#any(duplicated(bind))
#bind[duplicated(bind), ]
#df_unique <- bind[!duplicated(bind), ]
#bind <- df_unique

# save it
cumulative_file <- file.path(
  output_dir, "nsidc_sic_summary_v4",
  glue("sic_bootstrapv4_16pixels_01Nov-30Apr_{format(start_date, '%Y')}-{format(end_date, '%Y')}.csv")
)
safe_write_csv(bind, cumulative_file)
```

## Outputs

Running this script produces the following:

- **`eider16p`**: an in-session data frame with one row per pixel per successfully processed day within `start_date` to `end_date`, including `lon`, `lat`, projected `x`/`y` coordinates (EPSG:3411), `bs_sic_prop` (sea ice concentration, percent), and `sicDate` (date parsed from the source filename).
- **`error_log`**: a list of any GeoTIFFs within the requested date range that failed to load or extract, each with the associated error message, so failures can be investigated without re-running the entire batch.
- **A single-period CSV**, named from `start_date`/`end_date`: `output/sic_beringSea_16pixels/sic_bootstrapv4_16pixels_[start_date]_[end_date].csv`.
- **`all_previous`** (if a previous cumulative file exists at the expected path): the previously saved cumulative record, read back in for the append step.
- **`bind`**: either the combined data frame (`all_previous` + `eider16p`), or just `eider16p` alone if no previous cumulative file was found. Optionally de-duplicated if the commented-out duplicate-check lines are enabled.
- **An updated cumulative CSV**, named from `start_date`/`end_date`: `output/sic_beringSea_16pixels/nsidc_sic_summary_v4/sic_bootstrapv4_16pixels_01Nov-30Apr_[start_year]-[end_year].csv`.
- **Overwrite protection**: both CSV writes above go through `safe_write_csv()`. If a file already exists at the target path, the default (`overwrite_existing <- FALSE`) stops the script with an error rather than overwriting it; setting `overwrite_existing <- TRUE` instead renames the existing file aside with a timestamped `.bak_[timestamp]` suffix before writing the new one, so no prior output is ever lost.
